newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OTC shares fall in Singapore on settlement rumours.
newsitem.headline: OTC shares fall in Singapore on settlement rumours.

text.p: Several over-the-counter shares tumbled sharply in Singapore on Wednesday afternoon on rumours that the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) would shorten its settlement period during the next few days.

Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu announced last year the SES planned to shorten, in the first quarter of 1997, the period within which dealers must settle their share trading accounts to three days from five days.
He did not say exactly when the change would take place.
Brokers said rumours had spread through the market on Wednesday afternoon that the change might happen immediately.
This had worried some dealers who had large "contra", or unsettled, positions on speculative OTC shares.
A contra trade is where an investor buys a share in the hope of a quick gain, knowing the share can be resold before the end of the settlement period. The difference can then be pocketed.

"If the change was immediate, they might be left having to pay up for the shares instead of being able to sell them back in the market later," said one institutional broker. "That could be a problem, especially if they have insufficient funds."
Other dealers said they believed the settlement change may happen with effect from Friday, March 1.
Singapore's UOB OTC index closed down 4.97 points on Wednesday at 1,354.45.
